explain.say: Imagine you are walking home and a dog suddenly barks behind a gate. Before you even think, you jump! That jump is your body's ancient safety system. Look at the chain on the board. It starts with something scary.

explain.say: Now look at adrenaline. Two small glands on top of your kidneys, called adrenal glands, squirt out adrenaline, a chemical messenger. It makes your heart pound and gives your muscles quick energy. Have you ever felt your hands shake after a fright?

faq.a: Adrenaline is a chemical messenger made by the adrenal glands, which sit on top of your kidneys. It makes your heart beat faster and gives your muscles a quick burst of energy.
asks: What does adrenaline do to your body?
Why do I shake after a fright?

faq.a: Freezing is when your body goes very still, and you might not be able to move or speak for a moment. Animals do it to avoid being spotted. It is automatic, not something you choose.
asks: Why do I freeze when I am scared?

faq.q: How long does it take to calm down after a fright?
faq.a: The first rush fades in minutes, but adrenaline can keep you feeling jumpy for 20 minutes or more. Slow breathing and moving gently help your body settle sooner.
asks: Why do I still feel shaky after being scared?

faq.q: Why does my body react to a test like it is dangerous?
faq.a: Your brain's alarm cannot always tell a real danger from a big challenge. So a test or a performance can switch on the same body reaction as a barking dog.
asks: Why do I get scared before exams?

faq.q: Can I stop fight or flight from starting?
faq.a: You cannot stop it starting, because it is automatic. But you can help it end sooner by breathing slowly and telling yourself "I am safe right now".
asks: How do I calm fight or flight?

facts: The adrenal glands sit on top of the kidneys and release adrenaline when you are frightened.
American scientist Walter Cannon described the "fight or flight" response in the early 1900s.

quiz.say: Which chemical floods your body in fight or flight?
quiz.show: Which chemical floods your body in fight or flight?
quiz.why: Adrenaline from the adrenal glands makes your heart pound and powers up your muscles.

wrong.1: Saliva is spit in your mouth; your mouth often goes dry when scared.
wrong.2: Vitamin C comes from food like oranges, not from a fright.
